images.prompt:
Create one original premium photorealistic field-guide portrait of an anonymous mature Can de Chira, the living Aragonese Pyrenean herding type. Text-only factual synthesis, no input photograph or named source specimen likeness.

One mature medium functional Can de Chira male about44cm, robust agile square trunk and straight back, strong straight neck without dewlap, ample oval ribs and moderate abdominal rise. Small proportional lupoid wedge head with flat skull and straight moderate muzzle, neither broad, face/skull about4:5, moderate stop, black nose/lips/eyelids and ordinary dark slightly almond eyes not slits. Natural medium-high-set flat ears relaxed against sides, tips about outer eye height, falling forward over face when attentive; no erect prick ears or cropped ears. Strong well-aligned complete fore/hind limbs, rounded toes and black nails, unobtrusive natural dewclaws. Semi-long black coat with newly placed light grey/white face and muzzle/distal-limb points and two restrained round light grey spots above eyes; longer neck/underbelly/thigh/forearm furnishings, shorter head/trunk. Choose the expressly allowed complete full natural long tail, carried backward with gentle open saber curve, not docked, stump or tight ring; all root/course/free endpoint visible. No inference that photographed shortened tails are full; this selected full-tail form comes from literal RSCE text.

Invent a fresh relaxed standing left-facing three-quarter pose, head gently toward viewer and mouth closed. A broad level clear mountain-pasture footpath in the Aragonese Pyrenees, distant green foothills and gentle diffuse late-spring morning light. Entire developed head/ears/trunk, four coherent complete limb courses and four distinct grounded paws with believable joints, weight and contact shadows. Entire attached long tail through free endpoint separately readable against clear space. One dog only, no puppy, giant molosser or tiny toy proportions, cropped/prick ears, docked/stump tail, tight tail ring, missing/fused/extra limbs, collar, harness, people, livestock, props, text, logos, watermark or border. One finished image.

profileEvidence.summary: Can de Chira dogs are responsive, disciplined workers with a strong interest in livestock and a close bond with their handlers. This regional herding type from the Aragonese Pyrenees moves sheep and cattle, with sheep traditionally handled without biting. Its Aragonese name describes a dog that turns the flock, reflecting the task at the heart of its history.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Responsive Pyrenean herders that work closely with handlers, turning sheep and cattle through Aragón’s mountain pastures.
